narrative: Material PL1__M60E8727 exhibits intermittent, highly erratic demand (CV=1.41) with roughly 44% zero-demand working days and occasional large spikes up to ~1,432 units. Lead times are short (mean 0.35 days) but highly variable (CV=0.83), which together drive a safety stock of 226 units — more than double the current SAP setting of 107. The EOQ of 6,156 units is constrained by the 3,460-unit storage limit, resulting in an adjusted order quantity of 3,234 units; the (r,Q) policy with r=280 and Q=3,234 reduces annual ordering events from ~178 to ~12, saving approximately 91% in total annual replenishment costs.
warnings: EOQ (6156) exceeds max_storage_units (3459.607); order quantity capped at 3234 units (max_storage - safety_stock).
Safety stock increased from SAP value of 107 to 226 units to meet 95% service level.
Lead time coefficient of variation is high (0.83) — lead time instability is a key risk driver.
Storage utilization reaches 100% immediately after each replenishment — any unplanned demand surge before delivery poses a stockout risk.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Given intermittent but high-volume demand and a binding storage constraint, a continuous-review (r,Q) policy is appropriate: it triggers replenishment precisely when inventory hits the reorder point, avoiding the excess holding cost of periodic review while allowing a large, consolidating order quantity that dramatically reduces ordering frequency.
research_insights.boundary_risk: The storage capacity constraint reduces the order quantity from the unconstrained EOQ of 6,156 to 3,234 units. This doubles the number of annual replenishments (12 vs. ~6 at EOQ) and slightly increases ordering costs, but the constraint cannot be relaxed without a storage expansion decision. At peak stock, the warehouse is at 100% utilisation for this material, leaving no buffer for emergency receipts.
research_insights.escalation_flag: none — MOQ (222) + safety_stock (226) = 448, which is well within max_storage_units (3,460). No MOQ-capacity infeasibility exists.
